title: Japan's Births Increase for First Time in 11 Years
paragraphs: For many years, the number of babies born in Japan has been falling. But according to new government data, the number of births has finally increased, at least for now.

Japan's health ministry released preliminary figures in August 2026. They showed that 342,068 babies were born in the country between January and June 2026. This was 2,788 more than in the same period of 2025, an increase of 0.8%. It was the first time in 11 years that the number of births in the first half of the year had gone up compared with the year before.

These preliminary figures include babies born in Japan to foreign parents, as well as Japanese babies born overseas. In November, the government released another set of figures that counted only Japanese babies born in Japan. These figures also showed a small increase, of 1,379 births, or 0.4%.

Some experts believe the increase may be connected to a rise in the number of marriages after the COVID-19 pandemic. In the first half of 2026, there were 238,979 marriages, which was 0.2% more than a year earlier.

However, the good news should be seen in context. It was the fifth year in a row that the number of births in the first half of the year was below 400,000. For the whole year, Japan's births fell below 800,000 for the first time in 2022, and below 700,000 in 2024.

At the same time, many more people are dying than are being born. In the first half of 2026, 778,982 people died in Japan. This means that the population fell by 436,914 people because of the difference between births and deaths.
It is still too early to say whether this increase is the start of a long-term change in Japan's population trends.
